video.title: You Can Now Build Apps for Free With Google AI Studio (w/ Google Insider)

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Logan Kilpatrick, who leads the developer product team for Google AI Studio and the Gemini API at Google DeepMind. They discuss how vibe coding in AI Studio makes it nearly free to build and ship many small AI apps, and they live-build two apps: a video analysis engine and a voice AI lead-gen agent. Ideas covered include niche single-purpose AI apps, bundles of AI tools for one persona, an AI implementation agency for small businesses, voice AI agents and a text-based AI travel companion. Key takeaway: the cost of building software is now trivial, so take many niche shots, iterate through about 10 prompts, and use vibe-coded demos as outreach. Chris states this is not sponsored but he is a Google shareholder.

ideas.name: AI implementation agency for small businesses

acquisition_channels.details: Personalised outreach: vibe code a redesign of the prospect's website or products with AI and send it as a lead-gen demo, e.g. 'I redesigned your website using AI. Here it is.'

acquisition.how: Agents can generate demo redesigns, but UK PECR bars unsolicited outreach to sole traders, so outreach is limited to limited companies by email.

delivery.how: Vibe coding tools build most of each app, but iteration and client fit need human checks.

billing.how: Invoices and subscriptions can be automated.

support.how: Non-technical owners need hand-holding and change requests.

uk_applicability.notes: Works the same in the UK. Cold email only to limited companies under PECR; sole traders need consent.

lessons.lesson: When building software costs near zero, the winning strategy shifts from one big swing to many cheap experiments.

quote.text: the cost of building software is now trivial and like the strategy in which you should employ in that world looks very different than the conventional wisdom
quote.speaker: Logan Kilpatrick

lessons.lesson: Solving your own problems, where you have domain insight, gives the best odds, but outsiders sometimes find overlooked angles.
Err towards niches that feel too small; the real customer need is often one narrow task.
The moat is the product experience built around a commodity model, not the model itself.
Many decision makers, even senior executives, lack AI skills, which creates demand for implementation services.
Persistence and agency matter more than syntax knowledge; error messages build resilience.
A fast working demo of the prospect's own problem sells the idea's feasibility and beats a generic pitch.
New model launches spawn thousands of copycats on day one; differentiate via remixing, positioning and niche insight.
A portfolio of tools lets you cross-sell across lists, share ad accounts and infrastructure, and learn faster what customers want.

evidence_quality.rationale: Mostly speculative discussion and live demos from a Google product lead; few concrete business numbers, and the only revenue claims are second-hand (John Rush, levels.io). Chris has a brief first-hand voice-agent anecdote without numbers.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Logan promotes Google AI Studio (his employer's product) and Chris is a Google shareholder; the episode also includes ads for Go High Level and Chris's TK Owners community.
